solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Ostentatiously display fraternal love, initially, in front of relative

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each of the two words before it

parts.note: the opening letters of both words
an aunt is a relative

explanation.surface: Someone showing off their affection for a brother, then turning to another family member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In front of' places the two initials before the relative.
explanation.definitionFit: To flaunt something is to show it off showily, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Cosmetic treatment from female expert on the cards

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for female
an ace is a highly skilled person
a pack is a full set of playing cards

explanation.surface: A beauty treatment courtesy of a woman who reads fortunes in cards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' in a down clue puts one piece above the other, so the expert sits on top of the cards. 'On the cards' also suggests 'likely'.
explanation.definitionFit: A face pack is a cream or paste spread on the skin to cleanse it, a beauty treatment.

clue.text: Organise a run over series of mountains

parts.note: taken as written
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run
a range is a chain of mountains

explanation.surface: Setting up a run across a mountain chain.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' places the first pieces above the mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrange is to put things in order or plan them, a synonym of organise.

clue.text: Course that's what expanding company seeks

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a famous English racecourse in Suffolk
second meaning: a growing business looks for fresh customers in an untapped area

explanation.walkthrough: 'Course' sounds like a plan of action for the company, but it is a racecourse, home of the Guineas horse races.
explanation.definitionFit: Newmarket is a racecourse town, and a growing firm seeks a new market for its goods.

clue.text: Abridged volume is by Tolstoy, say, or British noble

parts.note: V is the short form of volume
taken as written
Leo Tolstoy held the title of Count; 'say' marks him as an example

explanation.surface: A shortened edition of a Tolstoy novel, offered as a choice beside some British aristocrat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abridged volume' tempts you to shorten a book title, but it is just the abbreviation V.
explanation.definitionFit: A viscount is a peer ranking between earl and baron in the British peerage.

clue.text: The writer will repeat point that's not a problem for reader

definitions.note: a cryptic twist: anyone who is a reader can by definition read

parts.note: the setter as 'I will', contracted
to iterate is to do or say again
a ness is a headland or promontory

explanation.surface: An author promising to restate a point that readers will not struggle with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The writer' is the crossword setter speaking of themself. The definition is wry: inability to read is the one thing a reader cannot suffer from.
explanation.definitionFit: Illiterateness is the inability to read, which by definition never troubles someone who reads.

clue.text: Note bullets set up for part of list, invariably

parts.note: C is a musical note

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means raised, so the word reads from the bottom upward

parts.note: ammo is short for ammunition

explanation.surface: Bullet points arranged as items in a list.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bullets' suggests bullet points in a list, but it means ammunition.
explanation.definitionFit: A comma separates the items whenever words are written as a list, so it always appears in one.

clue.text: Utter shambles surrounding church in European city

indicators.note: a shambles is a disordered mess, so these letters are jumbled
surrounding means the jumbled letters wrap around the next piece

parts.note: the letters rearranged
CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A total mess around a church somewhere in Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Utter' reads as an adjective meaning complete, but it is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Utrecht is a city in the central Netherlands.

clue.text: Take part in event and emphasise it's not normally what one rides

definitions.text: it's not normally what one rides
definitions.note: cryptic: this bicycle is built for two riders, not one

indicators.note: take part in says to take a section from inside the following words

parts.note: spans the end of the first word, the whole middle word, and the start of the last

explanation.surface: Advice to join a contest and stress something unusual about one's mount.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on 'one': a single person normally does not ride this bicycle alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A tandem is a bicycle with seats and pedals for two riders, so not one.

clue.text: Nostalgic chap mailed a catalogue, including old boys in it

parts.note: mail sent by post

indicators.note: in places the first group of men within the following word
including means the outer phrase takes the next part into its middle

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
a list is an itemised catalogue
old boys taken loosely as chaps, men

explanation.surface: A wistful man who posted a catalogue featuring former pupils.
explanation.walkthrough: Two layers of insertion: the men go into 'it', and that unit is included in the middle of 'mailed a catalogue'. 'Old boys' suggests former pupils, but means only men.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentimentalist is a person given to tender, nostalgic feeling.

clue.text: Revolutionary movement in West he introduced to political bloc

indicators.note: things introduced to a group go inside it, so the first pieces sit within the bloc

parts.note: a cartel is an alliance of parties or firms acting together
W is the abbreviation for west
taken as written

explanation.surface: A revolution in the West that some man brought into a political alliance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary movement' sounds political, but it is a gymnast's sideways roll, which literally revolves.
explanation.definitionFit: A cartwheel is a sideways handspring in which the body turns a full circle, so it is a movement that revolves.

clue.text: Fool's gold found in second excavation, finally

indicators.note: something found in another is sitting inside it

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second
or is the heraldic word for gold

indicators.note: finally picks out the closing letter of the word before it

parts.note: the closing letter of the word

explanation.surface: A dupe's gold, unearthed late in a second dig.
explanation.walkthrough: Fool's gold suggests iron pyrites, but 'Fool' alone is the definition and the 's means 'is'. Heraldry gives the word for gold here.
explanation.definitionFit: A moron is an insulting word for a stupid person, a synonym of fool.

clue.text: Object set in long piece of jewellery

indicators.note: a stone set in a mount is held inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: to pant for something is to long for it
an end is an aim or object

explanation.surface: An item mounted in a lengthy jewel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set in' and 'piece of jewellery' share a jeweller's scene, but 'long' is a verb, to yearn.
explanation.definitionFit: A pendant is an ornament hanging from a chain around the neck.

clue.text: Portion husband consumed in abstracted state

indicators.note: what is consumed in something ends up inside it

parts.note: a trance is a dazed, absent state of mind
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A husband eating his share while lost in thought.
explanation.definitionFit: A tranche is a slice or instalment of something, a share of a larger whole.

clue.text: Neck or lip, or nearby part of head

definitions.meaning: first meaning: both are slang for impudence
second meaning: the fleshy side of the face, near the neck and lip

explanation.walkthrough: Neck and lip read as body parts, but both are British slang for insolent talk; only the last part means the body part.
explanation.definitionFit: Impudence is called cheek, neck or lip, and the cheek is also the side of the face beside the mouth.

clue.text: Ethical system — test it in my case?

indicators.note: in says the preceding pieces are placed within what follows
a case holds something, so the word before it wraps around the others

parts.note: taken as written, split around the rest
an oral is a spoken examination
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone wondering whether ethics could be examined in their own situation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My case' reads as 'my situation', but the word my is the case that holds the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Morality is a code of right and wrong conduct, a system of ethics.

clue.text: Within the neighbourhood, housing foreign fighter in sensible fashion

indicators.note: housing something means giving it a home inside, so one piece shelters the other

parts.note: locally means nearby, in the area
a GI is an American soldier, foreign from a British view

explanation.surface: A local area sheltering an overseas soldier, done with good sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Logically means reasoning soundly, acting in a rational, sensible way.

clue.text: Odd piles rearranged, not evenly distributed

indicators.note: rearranged signals that the letters are put in a fresh order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Strange heaps restacked, still unbalanced.
explanation.definitionFit: Lopsided means leaning to one side, with weight unequally spread.

clue.text: Strict disciplinarian putting soldier outside time and time again

indicators.note: putting one thing outside another wraps it around that thing

parts.note: a marine is a seagoing soldier
T is the abbreviation for time
another T for time, added at the end

explanation.surface: A drill sergeant who keeps locking a soldier out time after time.
explanation.walkthrough: The first T goes inside the soldier; 'again' supplies a second T placed after.
explanation.definitionFit: A martinet is someone who demands rigid obedience to rules, named after a French drillmaster.

clue.text: Before PM starts, a vitality that's remarkable

parts.note: the morning, the hours before the afternoon begins
taken as written
zing is energy, liveliness

explanation.surface: A burst of energy before the Prime Minister begins speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: PM looks like the Prime Minister, but it is post meridiem, the afternoon.
explanation.definitionFit: Amazing means astonishing, causing great wonder, close in sense to remarkable.

clue.text: Enthusiastic enjoyment, something that blows over

parts.note: a gust is a sudden blast of wind
O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: Relishing something that soon blows over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blows over' reads as one phrase meaning passes, but it splits into a blowing thing and a cricket over.
explanation.definitionFit: Gusto is hearty relish or zest in doing something.

clue.text: As we're perturbed about temperature, producing warm garment

indicators.note: perturbed means agitated, so these letters are thrown into disorder
about means placed around, so the jumbled letters enclose the next piece

parts.note: the letters rearranged
T is the abbreviation for temperature

explanation.surface: Bothered by the cold, we put on something cosy.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface hints at the answer itself: worrying about temperature does make you sweat.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweater is a knitted jumper worn to keep warm.

clue.text: Old ruler commemorated in July or August

definitions.text: Old ruler commemorated in July or August

parts.note: surface reading: some ancient monarch honoured in summer
setter's reading: July is named for Julius and August for Augustus, who both bore this Roman title

explanation.surface: An ancient monarch remembered at a summer festival.
explanation.walkthrough: The months themselves are the memorials: July honours Julius and August honours Augustus.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman title was borne by Julius and by the emperor Augustus, whose names became months.

clue.text: Following style of president lacking capital in part of US

indicators.note: lacking its capital means the word loses its leading letter

parts.note: à la means in the manner of
Barack Obama, US president

explanation.surface: Copying a president's manner without any money, somewhere in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like money or a city, but it is the capital letter at the start of the president's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Alabama is one of the southern states of the USA.

clue.text: Like legal action, start off really bad

indicators.note: start off means the opening letter is taken away

parts.note: lawful means permitted by law

explanation.surface: A lawsuit that begins dreadfully.
explanation.definitionFit: Awful means terrible or very poor in quality.

clue.text: Original clue in paper put back as centrepiece?

indicators.note: something put back is turned the other way, so the newspaper's name is read backwards
in places the first word within the other piece

parts.note: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper

indicators.note: original can mean novel or inventive, so the word after it is given a new arrangement

parts.note: the letters of the word rearranged

explanation.surface: A first-draft clue in a newspaper reinstated as the main feature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Original' reads as 'first version', but it asks for a creative rearrangement. The question mark flags that 'centrepiece' is a loose definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A nucleus is the central core around which something is built, as of a cell or atom.

clue.text: Unfriendly, small, and petty quarrel

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small
a tiff is a minor squabble

explanation.surface: A cold, mean-spirited little squabble.
explanation.definitionFit: A stiff manner is formal and cold, lacking warmth toward others.

clue.text: Taking offence about article liable to be shocking? On the contrary

definitions.text: liable to be shocking? On the contrary

indicators.note: about means going around, so the first word encloses the article

parts.note: someone insulted has been given offence
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone offended by a piece that might cause a scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the contrary' flips 'liable to be shocking': the answer describes something protected from electric shocks.
explanation.definitionFit: Insulated wiring is covered in non-conducting material, so it will not give an electric shock.

clue.text: Get a rule revised to exercise control

indicators.note: a revised version is rewritten, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Getting a rule changed in order to keep things in check.
explanation.definitionFit: To regulate is to control or govern something by rules, a synonym.

clue.text: Like a mule held by lengthy bridle

indicators.note: held by says the answer is gripped inside the words that follow

parts.note: runs across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A mule restrained by a long harness strap.
explanation.definitionFit: A mule is the cross-bred offspring of a horse and a donkey, so it is of mixed breed.
